t: You're on Marsham Street, a street in the City of Westminster. It runs south for about a mile from Great Peter Street, near Victoria Street and Parliament Square. The street takes its name from Sir Robert Marsham, the fourth Baronet, who lived from 1650 to 1703. He was an English politician who sat in the House of Commons from 1698 to 1702. That's a short parliamentary career, but his name has outlasted it on the street signs.
